questions.text: The April 2025 militant attack that triggered the India-Pakistan crisis of that year took place at which location in Indian-administered Kashmir?
questions.explanation: The attack on tourists at Pahalgam on 22 April 2025 killed 26 people and set off the diplomatic and military escalation between India and Pakistan.

questions.text: India's military operation launched against Pakistan on 7 May 2025 was code-named:
questions.explanation: India named its 7 May 2025 missile and air strikes on Pakistan and Azad Kashmir 'Operation Sindoor'.

questions.text: Pakistan's retaliatory military operation launched on 10 May 2025 against India was code-named:
questions.explanation: Pakistan named its 10 May 2025 tri-services response 'Bunyan-um-Marsoos', a Quranic phrase meaning a firmly cemented structure.

questions.text: On which date did India launch Operation Sindoor against targets in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Operation Sindoor began in the early hours of 7 May 2025, about two weeks after the Pahalgam attack.

questions.text: The ceasefire that ended the May 2025 armed conflict between India and Pakistan took effect on:
questions.explanation: A ceasefire was announced and took effect on the evening of 10 May 2025, four days after hostilities began.

questions.text: The head of state who publicly announced the India-Pakistan ceasefire of 10 May 2025 before either government did was the president of:
questions.explanation: US President Donald Trump announced the ceasefire publicly on social media on 10 May 2025, crediting American mediation.

questions.text: In Pakistan's official terminology, the May 2025 armed conflict with India is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Pakistan officially designates the May 2025 conflict 'Marka-e-Haq' (the battle for truth); Bunyan-um-Marsoos was the name of the military operation within it.

questions.text: Which treaty did India announce it would hold 'in abeyance' after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack?
questions.explanation: India's Cabinet Committee on Security announced on 23 April 2025 that the Indus Waters Treaty would be held in abeyance with immediate effect.

questions.text: In its statement of 24 April 2025, Pakistan's National Security Committee said it reserved the right to hold which agreement in abeyance?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's National Security Committee responded to India's measures by stating it had the right to hold the 1972 Simla Agreement, and other bilateral accords, in abeyance.

questions.text: Pakistan's National Security Committee statement of 24 April 2025 declared that any attempt to stop or divert Pakistan's share of Indus waters would be treated as:
options: A breach of the UN Charter only
questions.explanation: The Committee stated that any attempt to stop or divert water belonging to Pakistan under the Indus Waters Treaty would be considered an act of war.

questions.text: Which body issued the supplemental award of 27 June 2025 holding that the Indus Waters Treaty does not permit a party to unilaterally place it in abeyance?
options: The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
The Court of Arbitration constituted under the Indus Waters Treaty
questions.explanation: The Court of Arbitration constituted under the Treaty, with the Permanent Court of Arbitration as registry, ruled on 27 June 2025 that India's abeyance did not affect the Court's competence.

questions.text: Which land crossing with Pakistan did India announce it was closing after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack?
questions.explanation: India ordered the closure of the Attari Integrated Check Post on the Attari-Wagah route as part of its 23 April 2025 measures.

questions.text: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, the three rivers allocated to Pakistan are:
questions.explanation: The Treaty gives Pakistan the western rivers - Indus, Jhelum and Chenab - while India receives the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

questions.text: The Indus Waters Treaty between Pakistan and India was signed in which year, with which institution as broker?
questions.explanation: The Treaty was signed in Karachi in September 1960 after negotiations brokered by the World Bank, which is also a signatory for limited purposes.

questions.text: Which Pakistan Army chief was promoted to the rank of Field Marshal on 20 May 2025?
questions.explanation: The federal cabinet approved the promotion of General Syed Asim Munir to Field Marshal on 20 May 2025, citing his leadership during the conflict with India.

questions.text: Asim Munir's elevation in May 2025 made him which Field Marshal in Pakistan's history?
questions.explanation: He became Pakistan's second Field Marshal; the first was Ayub Khan, who assumed the rank in 1959.

questions.text: The Pakistan-Afghanistan ceasefire of October 2025 was agreed at negotiations held in which city?
questions.explanation: After a week of the worst border fighting in years, Pakistani and Afghan delegations agreed to an immediate ceasefire at talks in Doha.

questions.text: Which two countries mediated the Pakistan-Afghanistan ceasefire agreed in October 2025?
questions.explanation: Qatar and Türkiye jointly mediated the Doha talks that produced the October 2025 ceasefire between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

questions.text: On what date was the Pakistan-Afghanistan ceasefire announced in Doha in 2025?
questions.explanation: The immediate ceasefire was announced on 19 October 2025, following clashes that began around 11 October.

questions.text: The follow-up rounds of Pakistan-Afghanistan negotiations after the October 2025 Doha ceasefire were hosted in which city?
questions.explanation: Follow-up talks intended to build mechanisms for a durable peace were held in Istanbul, and broke down in November 2025 without agreement.

questions.text: The boundary between Pakistan and Afghanistan, which Kabul has never formally recognised, is known as the:
questions.explanation: The Durand Line, demarcated in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan, remains the de facto Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

questions.text: The Torkham border crossing links Pakistan's Khyber district with which Afghan province?
questions.explanation: Torkham is the busiest Pakistan-Afghanistan crossing, connecting Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa with Nangarhar province.

questions.text: The Chaman border crossing connects Balochistan with which Afghan province?
questions.explanation: Chaman in Balochistan faces Spin Boldak in Kandahar province, making it the second-busiest crossing on the Durand Line.

questions.text: Pakistan's programme for the deportation of undocumented foreign nationals, under which large numbers of Afghans have been repatriated since 2023, is called the:
questions.explanation: The Illegal Foreigners Repatriation Plan, announced in late 2023, has been implemented in phases covering undocumented migrants and later Afghan Citizen Card holders.

questions.text: Pakistan's retaliatory strikes inside Iranian territory in January 2024 were code-named:
questions.explanation: Pakistan carried out Operation Marg Bar Sarmachar on 18 January 2024 against Baloch separatist hideouts inside Iran, two days after Iranian strikes on Pakistani soil.

questions.text: The Iranian strikes on Pakistani territory in January 2024 targeted alleged bases of which group?
questions.explanation: Iran said its 16 January 2024 strikes in Balochistan targeted the Sunni militant group Jaish al-Adl, which operates across the Iran-Pakistan border.

questions.text: Which Iranian president made a state visit to Pakistan in August 2025?
questions.explanation: President Masoud Pezeshkian visited Islamabad on 2-3 August 2025, holding talks with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on trade and border security.

questions.text: During the Iranian president's August 2025 visit to Islamabad, the two sides set a bilateral trade target of:
questions.explanation: Pakistan and Iran agreed to raise annual bilateral trade to US$10 billion from roughly US$3 billion at the time.

questions.text: The Taftan border crossing, Pakistan's main land route to Iran, lies in which province?
questions.explanation: Taftan is in Chagai district of Balochistan and faces Mirjaveh on the Iranian side.

questions.text: The flagship deep-sea port of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor is located at:
questions.explanation: Gwadar port in Balochistan is CPEC's flagship maritime project, operated under a Chinese concession.

questions.text: Pakistan hosted a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in October 2024 in which city?
questions.explanation: Islamabad hosted the 23rd meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government on 15-16 October 2024.

questions.text: Which Chinese leader represented China at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting hosted by Pakistan in October 2024?
questions.explanation: Premier Li Qiang led the Chinese delegation, as the Council of Heads of Government is a prime-ministerial-level SCO body.

questions.text: In 2025 Pakistan and China agreed to advance the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor into which stage?
options: The Belt and Road pilot stage
questions.explanation: During Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's China visit in 2025 the two governments reaffirmed an upgraded CPEC Phase-2, focused on industry, agriculture, mining and IT.

questions.text: The 2025 SCO Council of Heads of State summit attended by Pakistan's prime minister was held in which Chinese city?
questions.explanation: The SCO Heads of State summit was held in Tianjin on 31 August-1 September 2025, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif attended.

questions.text: Pakistan became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in which year?
questions.explanation: Pakistan and India were admitted as full SCO members at the Astana summit in June 2017, having earlier been observers.

questions.text: The trade agreement announced between Pakistan and the United States in July 2025 was presented as centring on joint development of Pakistan's:
questions.explanation: President Trump announced the deal by highlighting cooperation on developing Pakistan's oil reserves alongside tariff relief for Pakistani exports.

questions.text: The reciprocal tariff rate applied to Pakistani exports under the United States order of July 2025 was:
questions.explanation: Pakistan's rate was set at 19 percent, lower than the 25 percent applied to India and 20 percent to Bangladesh at the time.

questions.text: In March 2025 Pakistan handed over to the United States a suspect accused of planning which attack?
options: The Abbey Gate bombing at Kabul airport
questions.explanation: Pakistan captured and transferred Mohammad Sharifullah, an Islamic State-Khorasan operative accused of planning the August 2021 Abbey Gate bombing that killed 13 US service members.

questions.text: In June 2025 the Government of Pakistan announced it would formally recommend which figure for the Nobel Peace Prize?
questions.explanation: Pakistan announced in June 2025 that it would nominate US President Donald Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize, citing his role in the May 2025 India-Pakistan ceasefire.

questions.text: Which Pakistani military officer was hosted for a working lunch at the White House by President Trump in June 2025?
options: Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu
questions.explanation: Field Marshal Asim Munir was received at the White House in June 2025, an unusual honour for a serving army chief without a head of government present.

questions.text: In December 2025 the Export-Import Bank of the United States approved financing of about US$1.25 billion for which Pakistani project?
questions.explanation: US EXIM approved roughly US$1.25 billion in financing for the Reko Diq mining project, part of a wider debt package involving the IFC and ADB.

questions.text: The Reko Diq copper and gold project, central to Pakistan's minerals diplomacy, is located in which province?
questions.explanation: Reko Diq lies in Chagai district of Balochistan and is operated by Barrick alongside federal and provincial government shareholdings.

questions.text: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement in September 2025 in which city?
questions.explanation: The agreement was signed at Al-Yamamah Palace in Riyadh on 17 September 2025 during Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's visit.

questions.text: Who signed the Pakistan-Saudi Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement of September 2025 on behalf of Saudi Arabia?
questions.explanation: Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman signed for Saudi Arabia, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signing for Pakistan.

questions.text: The central clause of the Pakistan-Saudi Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement of 2025 states that:
options: Neither state may host foreign military bases
Both states will jointly develop nuclear energy
Each will station a permanent brigade in the other
Any aggression against either country shall be considered aggression against both
questions.explanation: The agreement provides that aggression against either country shall be regarded as aggression against both, echoing collective-defence language.

questions.text: Which UAE head of state made his first official visit to Pakistan as president in December 2025?
options: Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan
Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum
Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed
questions.explanation: President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan made his first official visit to Pakistan as UAE head of state in December 2025.

questions.text: Pakistan's prime minister attended the October 2025 Gaza peace summit held at which Egyptian city?
questions.explanation: The summit co-chaired by President Trump and President Sisi was held at Sharm el-Sheikh on 13 October 2025, with Shehbaz Sharif among the attending leaders.

questions.text: Pakistan began a two-year term as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council covering which period?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's term as a non-permanent member of the Security Council runs from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2026.

questions.text: In the General Assembly election of June 2024, Pakistan won its Security Council seat with how many votes?
questions.explanation: Pakistan secured 182 votes in the UN General Assembly, comfortably above the required two-thirds majority.

questions.text: The 2025-2026 term is Pakistan's how-manieth term as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council?
questions.explanation: It is Pakistan's eighth term on the Security Council, one of the highest totals among Asian states.

questions.text: Pakistan held the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council during which month of 2025?
questions.explanation: Pakistan assumed the Security Council presidency for July 2025, the first of its two presidencies during the 2025-2026 term.

questions.text: Which Security Council resolution on strengthening mechanisms for the peaceful settlement of disputes was adopted unanimously under Pakistan's presidency in July 2025?
questions.explanation: Resolution 2788, sponsored by Pakistan, was adopted unanimously on 22 July 2025 during its Council presidency.

questions.text: Who chaired the high-level Security Council debate on multilateralism and peaceful settlement of disputes for Pakistan in July 2025?
options: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar
questions.explanation: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar presided over the signature events of Pakistan's July 2025 Council presidency.

questions.text: In June 2025 Pakistan was appointed chair of the Security Council sanctions committee established under which resolution?
questions.explanation: Pakistan chairs the committee created by Resolution 1988 (2011), which oversees sanctions measures relating to the Taliban.

questions.text: Alongside chairing the Taliban sanctions committee, Pakistan was appointed vice-chair of which Security Council body for 2025?
options: The Committee on Admission of New Members
questions.explanation: Pakistan was made a vice-chair of the Counter-Terrorism Committee, which monitors implementation of Resolution 1373 (2001).

questions.text: Who succeeded Munir Akram as Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in 2025?
questions.explanation: Asim Iftikhar Ahmad presented his credentials as Pakistan's Permanent Representative in April 2025 and led the mission during the July 2025 Council presidency.

questions.text: The 17th ECO Summit, attended by Pakistan's prime minister in July 2025, was held in which city?
questions.explanation: Azerbaijan hosted the 17th Economic Cooperation Organization summit at Khankendi on 3-4 July 2025.

questions.text: The permanent secretariat of the Economic Cooperation Organization, of which Pakistan is a founding member, is located in:
questions.explanation: The ECO secretariat is in Tehran; the organisation was founded in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as successor to the RCD.

questions.text: The 51st session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers, attended by Pakistan in June 2025, was hosted by which city?
questions.explanation: Türkiye hosted the 51st OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Istanbul on 21-22 June 2025 under the theme 'The OIC in a Transforming World'.

questions.text: The General Secretariat of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: The OIC General Secretariat has been based in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, pending the liberation of Jerusalem.

questions.text: The most recent SAARC summit actually held was the 18th, convened in which capital?
questions.explanation: The 18th SAARC summit was held in Kathmandu in November 2014; no summit has been held since.

questions.text: The 19th SAARC summit, indefinitely postponed after several members withdrew, was scheduled to be hosted by which city?
questions.explanation: Islamabad was to host the 19th SAARC summit in November 2016, but it was postponed after India and other members pulled out.

questions.text: The 11th D-8 Summit, attended by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in December 2024, was held in which city?
questions.explanation: Egypt hosted the 11th summit of the D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation in Cairo in December 2024 and assumed its chairmanship.

questions.text: Which head of state visited Pakistan in February 2025 for a meeting of the High Level Strategic Cooperation Council, during which 24 documents were exchanged?
options: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan of Türkiye
questions.explanation: Turkish President Erdogan visited Islamabad on 12-13 February 2025 for the Pakistan-Türkiye High Level Strategic Cooperation Council.

questions.text: Azerbaijan signed an investment agreement with Pakistan on the sidelines of the July 2025 ECO Summit worth approximately:
questions.explanation: Azerbaijan committed about US$2 billion of investment in Pakistan under an agreement signed during the Khankendi ECO Summit.

questions.text: Which European head of state paid an official visit to Pakistan in November 2024, the first by a leader of his country in decades?
options: Milos Zeman of the Czech Republic
questions.explanation: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko visited Pakistan on 25-27 November 2024, and several bilateral agreements were signed.

questions.text: In July 2025 Pakistan and Russia signed an agreement in Moscow to revive which industrial facility?
questions.explanation: The agreement, signed at Pakistan's embassy in Moscow, provides for Russian participation in restarting and expanding Pakistan Steel Mills in Karachi.

questions.text: Ishaq Dar's visit to Dhaka in August 2025 was the first by a Pakistani foreign minister since which year?
questions.explanation: It was described as the first visit by a Pakistani foreign minister to Bangladesh since 2012, and marked a thaw in bilateral ties.

questions.text: In 2025 Pakistan established diplomatic relations, for the first time, with which country through an exchange of a joint communique at Tianjin?
questions.explanation: Pakistan and Armenia exchanged a joint communique establishing diplomatic relations in 2025, ending Islamabad's long-standing non-recognition of Armenia.

questions.text: Who was appointed Foreign Secretary of Pakistan in September 2024, becoming only the second woman to hold the office?
questions.explanation: Amna Baloch took charge as Foreign Secretary in September 2024, following Tehmina Janjua as the second woman in the post.
